guide.summary: A budding yeast that eats sugar without needing oxygen and makes the water around it more sour.
guide.biology: Real yeasts can break down sugar without oxygen, called fermentation, which gives them less energy from each bite and can leave their surroundings more acidic.
guide.rules: Lives in water or gel and does not swim. Eats sugar without using oxygen, gaining 18 energy per carbon instead of 30, and adds 0.20 acid for every carbon it eats, which lowers the local pH. Oxygen neither helps nor slows it. Comfortable at pH 4.5 to 7, warmth 0.30 to 0.65 and salinity up to 0.25. Fungal inhibitor affects it. Buds off a daughter once it has doubled its body, is at least 25 seconds old and has spare energy. Prey for Amoeba and Rotifer.
guide.example: Put Bubbles on a sugar patch beside some Sprinters and watch the pH fall as the Bubbles spread.
